pr_title: Guard against db corruption when renaming entities
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Guard against db corruption when renaming entities

- Add a the `filter_unique_constraint_integrity_error` safeguard to the entity registry rename
- Add the same safe guard we had in the states meta manager to the statistics meta manager
- Fix commit before and ensure it works as all our tests ran with a commit interval of zero

issue_context.title: Energy dashboard statistics stop recording, then database corruption (sqlite)
issue_context.body:

HA stops recording long term statistics. After restart of HA the database file is marked as corrupted and a fresh database is created. All long-term statistics are consquently gone. Short-term statistics work fine and are current.

`PRAGMA schema.integrity_check;` on the old database file returns no errors.

When I go back to `core-2024.1.6` using the old db all long term statistics are back. The database file is not recreated.

core-2024.2.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2024.1.6

Home Assistant Container

I would be very happy if I could save my past history and not have to start from scratch again. This would be the second time that I have lost the database since I started using HA.

As far as I can tell, I have some rows in the database that cause problems. Unfortunately, the error message is too unspecific, and I don't know where to even look for the problematic data.

I think I found the problem. There were around 14K rows at the beginning of the  `statistics_short_term` table from early January that had a different format than the more recent ones. The old rows had the `created` and `start` columns populated with DATETIME values and empty (NULL) `created_ts` and `start_ts` columns. I'm guessing that these rows are a leftover from a schema change and migration, but I haven't investigated this further.

After clearing the old rows out with a simple SQL query, HA started without the error messages 🤗. The missing values on the energy dashboard started appearing again, probably because the calculation of 'long-term statistics' resumed. I still have a glitch on one of the daily graphs with two outlier values in two consecutive hour brackets (one positive, one negative), but that's a minor problem I can live with.

What is very strange, is that the old rows did not cause any problems until Febuary 27th, when the database crashed the first time completely with a scary `sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError` message. Off course it's possible that some unrelated event caused the error. It's very hard for me to judge.
I added a whole set of safeguards in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/112718 that should make it nearly impossible to get into this state
Sounds great! I'm happy I could contribute a tiny bit to make HA even more robust.
